messages_body:
Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

Summary of needs (from the call):
- Latency targets: p50 <= 100ms, p95 <= 300ms (for 512-token responses)
- Throughput: sustained 250 reqs/min with 1k-token average workload across parallel clients
- Concurrency: support for 50 concurrent sessions without p95 degradation
- Streaming: client requires token-level streaming with <50ms per-chunk delivery for interactive workflows
- Reproducibility: deterministic prompt sets and measurement harness usable by both teams

Proposed benchmark methodology (attachments):
- redwood-benchmark-plan-v1.pdf — high-level plan and roles
- prompt-set-edgefin.csv — initial prompt/metadata set (anonymized customer queries)
- eval-harness-readme.md (attached in follow-up) — how to run the harness locally / in-edgefin infra

Immediate next steps:
1) Alex / EdgeFin: confirm the prompt set is representative or share additional examples by EOD Friday 9/3.
2) Redwood (Marissa + Eng): finalize the harness README and a reproducible results template; share a Drive folder with scripts (linked below).
3) Schedule a 90-min run during your non-peak window (you proposed 9/8 — propose 09:00 PT) so we can collect p50/p95, tail latencies, and streaming chunk timing.
4) If you want, we can run an initial smoke benchmark on Redwood-hosted infra and compare results before moving to your infra.

A few measurement clarifications we discussed:
- Latency measuring point: token emit time at application socket (not just server internal completion)
- Streaming measurement: measure per-chunk inter-arrival times and time-to-first-token
- Warmup: include a 5-minute warmup and discard those samples

Attaching the prompt set we captured in the call; please mark any rows you want excluded. I added a lightweight results-template.csv to make comparisons reproducible.

Thanks — cc'ing Rishi and Lauren so the eng/sales teams are aligned on timing.

Best,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0199

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- The latency targets look reasonable; for our internal SLA we'll need p95 <= 250ms for short-form dialog (<=256 tokens). For longer responses we can accept relaxed p95 but would like to see streaming start within 150ms.
- We can run the harness on our staging cluster — we'll need the exact scripts and a docker image if possible.
- 9/8 09:00 PT works for initial run; can you confirm timezone for everyone? (looks like PT on your side).

A small ask: can you include a column in the prompt set that tags streaming vs batch expectations per prompt? That will help our SRE prioritize test runs.

I'll loop in our SRE alias for scheduling.

--Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform, EdgeFin
alex.johnson@edgefin.com

Looping back with a note from eng: we should be explicit about the reproducibility constraints. Two quick operational asks:

1) Please include the exact model + tokenizer versions (or the model hash) used in the run — we can't compare across runs otherwise.
2) For streaming, we'll instrument client-side timestamps; Redwood should provide a simple client harness (docker image) that outputs per-chunk timestamps to stdout in a CSV format matching results-template.csv.

I added Lauren for kernel/memory sizing questions — she can weigh in on whether 50 concurrent sessions maps to N GPUs or requires sharding/batching changes.

Rishi (sales) — can you confirm you'd like us to offer an initial hosted smoke test vs going straight to customer infra? We can offer a hosted smoke (10–20 min) to tune measurement pipeline.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — nice cross-functional momentum. Finalizing plan below (short checklist for the run):

Run checklist (what Redwood will deliver before 9/8):
- eval-harness-readme.md (attached): how to build/run harness, docker image tag, and environment variables.
- docker image: redwood/eval-harness:20260830 (contains client instrumented to emit per-chunk timestamps).
- prompt-set-edgefin.csv (attached) with new column "streaming_expected" added — please update any rows you want excluded.
- results-template.csv (attached) with headers: run_id, model, model_hash, prompt_id, token_count, latency_first_token_ms, latency_last_token_ms, p50_ms, p95_ms, throughput_rps, chunk_mean_ms, chunk_p95_ms

Day-of plan (9/8 09:00 PT):
- 09:00–09:10: quick sync (roll call + scope)
- 09:10–09:25: warmup (discarded)
- 09:25–09:55: steady-state run (collect samples)
- 09:55–10:10: lift results, sanity checks, initial comparison against SLOs
- Post-run: Redwood will upload raw CSVs to the shared Drive folder and a short summary PDF with charts.

Measurement definitions (short):
- Latency: measured at client socket from request send to first/last token arrival.
- Throughput: successful final responses / minute over the steady-state window.
- Concurrency: number of concurrently open sessions during steady-state — we will target 50 unless EdgeFin asks to scale.
- Streaming: per-chunk inter-arrival time; time-to-first-token must be reported separately.

Reproducibility notes:
- Use provided docker image and model hash; share any env overrides in a small .env file in the Drive folder.
- Seed prompts and PRNG seeds (where applicable) will be recorded in results metadata.

Please confirm the 9/8 09:00 PT slot and whether you'd like the hosted smoke test beforehand (we recommend it to validate the harness). I'll upload the harness README and the docker image tag + Drive folder by EOD today.

Best,
